proposal: The Mandate says enhanced statutory authority for local autonomy should extend to prioritizing rental subsidies that emphasize choice and mobility in vouchers over site-based subsidies, and to giving public housing agencies maximal flexibility to direct land sales involving existing public housing so land can be put to greater economic use. It asks Congress to consider the future of the public housing model, doubting that new investment beyond maintenance serves upward mobility, while cautioning that the turn to mobility vouchers must not come at the expense of local autonomy.

status_summary: No statute or executive action was found that gives public housing agencies broad authority to direct sales of public housing land or that prioritizes mobility-oriented vouchers over site-based subsidies, so the steps found are parallel to the recommendation. On 2026-07-11 Public Law 119-101 removed the end date of the Rental Assistance Demonstration and raised its public housing conversion cap from 455,000 to 555,000 units (section 212), moving more public housing to other rental assistance platforms; its table of contents lists no section on public housing disposition, land sales or voucher mobility, and a CRS summary describes none. HUD Notice PIH 2026-23, issued 2026-08-28 under existing Section 18 authority, eased demolition and disposition rules, including a very-small-PHA threshold of 75 or fewer units and functional obsolescence as a basis, while requiring fair market value for sales unless HUD approves a below-market transaction, and it sets terms for ground leases and disposal of excess vacant land. HUD's FY2027 budget justification (request submitted 2026-04-03, per CRS) proposes language barring public housing agencies, including Moving to Work agencies, from issuing any new vouchers or otherwise assisting new families in 2027, with exceptions for HUD-VASH, family unification, existing project-based leases and new RAD commitments, which runs against the mobility emphasis.

timeline.event: The FY2027 budget request is submitted to Congress (CRS); HUD's justification for tenant-based rental assistance proposes barring public housing agencies, including Moving to Work agencies, from issuing any new vouchers or otherwise assisting new families in 2027, with exceptions for HUD-VASH, Family Unification Program vouchers, leasing under existing project-based contracts and new RAD project-based commitments.

The novoco account gives the earlier very-small-PHA threshold as 50 units; the notice itself does not state the prior figure. No bill on PHA land sales was searched on congress.gov. In the 2026-10-17 review the enrolled text of Public Law 119-101 was read on GovInfo through section 212 together with the full table of contents; the later titles (including section 505 on a new Moving to Work cohort and section 805 on public housing agency accountability) were not read in full, but no table of contents title refers to disposition, land sales, vouchers or mobility. Notice PIH 2026-23 was read in full and states that it clarifies guidance under existing Section 18 of the 1937 Act and 24 CFR part 970 without new statutory authority. HUD's FY2027 justification for tenant-based rental assistance prints no date; the 2026-04-03 date is the submission date of the request given by CRS Report R48927, which does not mention the voucher limit.
